question: What long-term issue can happen if severe uterine infections leave behind scar tissue?

options.A: Complete loss of bladder control
options.B: Infertility or menstrual problems
options.C: Enlargement of the external genitalia
options.D: Permanent cessation of all hormones

explanation: Scars inside the uterus (adhesions) can mess up monthly periods and make it much harder for a woman to get pregnant in the future. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T20#GNS216_U5_T20_h8)

question: What is the main danger of feeding a severely malnourished patient too quickly?

options.A: Sudden permanent loss of all digestive enzyme production
options.B: Immediate development of chronic kidney stone formation
options.C: Dangerous drops in key electrolytes like potassium and phosphate
options.D: Rapid hardening of the major arteries in the neck

explanation: Sudden food intake shifts electrolytes into cells too fast, which can shock the heart if we aren't careful. Slow and steady wins the race here! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h8)

question: When a nurse gently pinches the skin to check hydration (skin turgor), which fibers in the dermis make the skin snap back?

options.A: Sebum and sweat secretions
options.B: Collagen and elastin fibers
options.C: Melanin and keratin proteins
options.D: Adipose and nervous tissues

explanation: Brilliant! Collagen and elastin give the dermis its spring and flexibility, helping nurses quickly check if a patient is well-hydrated. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T1#GNS213_U5_T1_h7)

question: What do we mean by 'socioeconomic determinants of health'?

options.A: Blood pressure readings taken at annual checkups
options.B: Income level, education, and living conditions
options.C: The specific surgical tools used in major hospitals
options.D: Genetic mutations inherited from biological parents

explanation: These are the social and money-related factors—like how much money you make, where you live, and your education—that heavily shape your health. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T9#GNS122_U3_T9_h4)

question: Why is it strongly preferred to give vasopressors through a central line rather than a peripheral vein?

options.A: Leaking into surrounding tissues can cause severe tissue damage and necrosis
options.B: Central lines deliver medication directly to the kidneys faster
options.C: Vasopressors dissolve peripheral plastic catheters very quickly
options.D: Peripheral veins are completely unable to absorb liquid medications

explanation: Vasopressors cause such intense blood vessel constriction that any leakage outside a peripheral vein cuts off local blood supply and destroys tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h7)

question: Which mental health issue is most commonly diagnosed in survivors of severe violence?

options.A: Bipolar mood disorder
options.B: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
options.D: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)

explanation: Correct! Survivors of intense physical, emotional, or sexual trauma very often develop PTSD because of the deep impact of their experience. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T14#GNS313_U3_T14_h4)

question: Why is it important to teach patients to finish all prescribed drops even if they feel better?

options.A: Stopping early can allow the infection to return stronger
options.B: Unused drops will expire quickly on the bathroom shelf
options.C: Leftover drops can cause severe poisoning if saved
options.D: Doctors require empty bottles brought back to the clinic

explanation: Stopping medication early before all bacteria or inflammation is cleared often causes the condition to flare up again. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h9)

question: In which hospital units are nurses most likely to use the intraperitoneal route?

options.A: Pediatric general medical wards
options.B: Oncology and peritoneal dialysis units
options.C: Routine outpatient vaccination clinics
options.D: Orthopedic rehabilitation centers

explanation: Spot on! You'll mostly see IP administration when caring for kidney patients doing peritoneal dialysis or cancer patients receiving special belly chemotherapy. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why do adult males typically have a higher resting metabolic rate than females of the same size?

options.A: Their digestive tract is physically longer
options.B: Their baseline body temperature is higher
options.C: Their brains require more glucose hourly
options.D: They generally have a higher percentage of lean muscle mass

explanation: Great job thinking through this! Men naturally tend to have more muscle mass than women, and since muscle burns more calories at rest, their baseline calorie need is higher. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h4)

question: Why is synovial fluid usually drawn from an inflamed joint?

options.A: To permanently cure chronic osteoarthritis
options.B: To measure the total blood volume of the patient
options.C: To inject air into the joint space for better movement
options.D: To discover the underlying cause of swelling and pain

explanation: Analyzing the aspirated fluid helps doctors identify infection, crystal diseases like gout, or inflammation. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h1)

question: How does pulmonary tuberculosis usually spread from one person to another?

options.A: By sharing eating utensils
options.B: Through direct skin-to-skin contact
options.C: Through contaminated drinking water
options.D: By airborne droplet nuclei

explanation: TB travels through tiny droplets in the air when someone with active TB coughs or sneezes. That's why breathing the same enclosed air can lead to infection. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h2)

question: How can rural communities creatively solve the problem of getting sick patients to a clinic?

options.A: Organizing local emergency transport systems like tricycles
options.B: Waiting for ambulances to be stationed in every street
options.C: Demanding that the government buy cars for every family
options.D: Building major federal highways to connect every village

explanation: Spot on! Communities often band together to arrange local transport like branded tricycles or bikes to bridge the gap during emergencies. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T3#GNS124_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which government bodies usually set the rules for healthcare waste management?

options.A: Ministries of health and environmental agencies
options.B: Patient advocacy groups and volunteer clubs
options.C: Local taxi drivers unions and market associations
options.D: Private pharmaceutical manufacturing companies

explanation: Well done! Government health and environmental sectors hold the legal duty to set safety standards for everyone. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h3)

question: Why is it so important to quickly isolate a suspected Ebola patient in a clinic?

options.A: It allows the lab to make local drugs
options.B: It prevents the virus from spreading to other patients and healthcare staff
options.C: It eliminates the need to wear protective gowns
options.D: It cures the patient before bleeding starts

explanation: Spot on! Isolating patients cuts off the transmission chain immediately and keeps everyone else in the ward safe. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h4)

question: When would a nurse researcher choose a qualitative design?

options.A: To test a specific drug dosage on a group of people
options.B: To prove cause and effect using large numerical samples
options.C: To quickly measure blood pressure across a large population
options.D: To explore the emotional details of a patient's illness

explanation: Great thinking! We use qualitative designs when we want rich, descriptive stories about human experiences instead of cold numbers. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T5#GNS224_U1_T5_h1)

question: What does 'cultural humility' mean for a home health nurse?

options.A: Recognizing personal biases and respecting the patient's cultural beliefs
options.B: Ignoring cultural differences to treat everyone identically
options.C: Reading a textbook about a culture before every visit
options.D: Convincing the patient to adopt the nurse's personal lifestyle

explanation: It's all about checking your own biases at the door and keeping an open mind about how a patient's background shapes their health choices. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h5)

question: A nurse assesses an adult patient with suspected acute osteomyelitis. Which set of findings is most expected?

options.A: Yellowing of the eyes, dark urine, and severe abdominal cramping
options.B: High fever, localized bone pain, swelling, and extreme tenderness
options.C: Numbness in both hands, low blood pressure, and a dry cough
options.D: Painless joint stiffness, dry skin, and generalized hair loss

explanation: Acute osteomyelitis classically triggers both systemic signs of infection like fever and distinct local signs like pain, warmth, and swelling at the bone site. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the main medical treatment for long-term (chronic) hypoparathyroidism?

options.A: Intravenous calcitonin injections given twice daily
options.B: High-dose potassium replacement therapy
options.C: Oral calcium supplements combined with active vitamin D
options.D: Daily doses of oral bisphosphonates to protect bones

explanation: Since the body isn't making enough PTH on its own, patients take oral calcium and active vitamin D as a tag-team effort to keep blood calcium stable. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T11#GNS222_U2_T11_h7)

question: Why might a family living in severe poverty choose not to spend money on transport to a family planning clinic?

options.A: Hospitals do not allow poor people inside
options.B: Medical clinics only open during midnight hours
options.C: They prefer buying luxury items for their home
options.D: Immediate daily survival needs take priority over preventive care

explanation: Exactly. When daily food and shelter are a struggle, spending scarce cash on transport for health checkups has to wait. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T006#GNS226_U6_T006_h6)

question: What main physical change happens inside the kidneys during chronic glomerulonephritis?

options.A: Sudden kidney enlargement
options.B: Rapid bacterial infection
options.C: Severe internal bleeding
options.D: Scarring of the glomeruli

explanation: You've got this! Chronic glomerulonephritis causes long-term damage that leads to glomerulosclerosis—which is just a fancy medical word for permanent scarring of the kidney's filtering units. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T5#GNS213_U4_T5_h1)

question: What is a major objective of public health surveillance programs?

options.A: Detecting epidemics early to stop transmission
options.B: Reducing the cost of medical equipment
options.C: Increasing the number of hospital beds
options.D: Providing free medications to the public

explanation: Early detection allows health workers to step in quickly and block the spread of infection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h2)

question: How do lab staff figure out if an antibiotic can kill a specific bacterium on a test plate?

options.A: By counting how many days the culture plate sat inside the incubator
options.B: By observing if the entire agar plate changes to a bright red color
options.C: By checking the expiration date printed on the exterior box of disks
options.D: By measuring the clear ring of no growth around the antibiotic disk

explanation: That clear halo around the antibiotic disk is called the zone of inhibition. The bigger the ring, the better the drug works! [learn more](GST114_U5_T4#GST114_U5_T4_h6)

question: You notice clear fluid draining from the nose of a patient who just had pituitary surgery. What is a quick bedside test to see if it is cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)?

options.A: Smell the fluid to check for a sharp ammonia or vinegar odor.
options.B: Check the exact temperature of the fluid with a digital probe.
options.C: Shine an ultraviolet light directly onto the wet dressing.
options.D: Test the fluid for glucose using a standard urine dipstick.

explanation: CSF is rich in glucose, whereas normal nasal mucus is not! Touching a glucose test strip to the drainage is a fast, clever way at the bedside to check for a CSF leak. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T9#GNS222_U2_T9_h8)

question: You are nursing a patient undergoing chemotherapy who has a dangerously low white blood cell count. What is your top priority action?

options.A: Practicing strict hand hygiene and enforcing protective isolation measures
options.B: Encouraging the patient to eat fresh, unwashed raw fruits and salads daily
options.C: Avoiding all vital sign checks to prevent disturbing the resting patient
options.D: Allowing large groups of visitors to visit at any time to boost morale

explanation: When white blood cell counts are down, the body's defense shield is lowered. Rigorous hand hygiene and protective isolation are vital to keep everyday environmental germs away from them. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h8)

question: Why do we carry an antiseptic solution like chlorhexidine in the infection prevention pack?

options.A: To act as an energy drink for tired mothers in labor
options.B: To serve as a nice jelly for easing dryness
options.C: To clean and prep the skin before exams or procedures
options.D: To quickly wipe down and clean rusty metal scissors

explanation: Antiseptic solutions lower the number of germs on the skin, which protects the mother and baby from nasty infections during delivery. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T10#GNS225_U3_T10_h2)

question: Which brain structure releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to start the cycle?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Pituitary gland
options.C: Adrenal gland
options.D: Thyroid gland

explanation: The hypothalamus is the master control center that secretes gonadotropin-releasing hormone to trigger the pituitary gland. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which clinical signs are classic clues that a patient's liver is struggling to excrete bilirubin properly?

options.A: Dark urine and pale, clay-colored stools
options.B: Extreme sensitivity to bright outdoor light
options.C: Bright red spots scattered over the chest
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

explanation: Think about the pathway: if bile can't reach the intestines, stool loses its brown colour, and the excess bilirubin spills out through the kidneys, making the urine very dark. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h4)

question: How does sucralfate protect an ulcer in the stomach?

options.A: Binding to ulcer craters to form a protective physical barrier
options.B: Neutralizing stomach acid directly through chemical reactions
options.C: Shutting down the proton pumps inside gastric parietal cells
options.D: Stopping histamine release from local immune system cells

explanation: Sucralfate turns into a sticky, protective paste when it hits stomach acid, gluing itself right over the sore like a Band-Aid! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h5)

question: Who discovered penicillin, our first natural antibiotic?

options.A: Joseph Lister
options.B: Edward Jenner
options.C: Paul Ehrlich
options.D: Alexander Fleming

explanation: Fleming spotted mold growing on a stray petri dish, and noticed it killed the surrounding bacteria. A lucky accident that changed medicine forever! [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h5)

question: How do bulk-forming laxatives primarily work to relieve constipation?

options.A: By absorbing water to increase stool size and softness
options.B: By directly irritating the colon wall to force contractions
options.C: By killing bacteria that dry out the stool
options.D: By coating the rectum with oil for easy passage

explanation: Bulk-forming agents swell up by drawing in water, which creates a larger, softer stool that triggers stretch receptors in the bowel. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T6#GNS212_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why should nurses be quick to spot the difference between side effects and true adverse drug reactions?

options.A: To know which symptoms require immediate clinical action versus routine monitoring
options.B: To ensure the patient stops paying for their hospital admission
options.C: To calculate the exact lethal dose for the patient chart
options.D: To prevent the hospital pharmacy from purchasing the drug again

explanation: Catching harm early lets you protect your patient fast and report things properly. Brilliant nursing care in action! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T5#GNS215_U2_T5_h1)

question: A young man is rushed to the emergency ward after sniffing petrol from a container. What immediate danger should you watch out for?

options.A: Chronic kidney stone formation and severe bone pain
options.B: Sudden permanent blindness from optic nerve damage
options.C: Immediate high blood pressure and rapid weight gain
options.D: Respiratory depression and central nervous system toxicity

explanation: Inhalants like petrol quickly slow down the brain, which can dangerously stop a person from breathing properly. Always monitor the airway first! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T11#GNS125_U2_T11_h3)

question: How is an adverse drug reaction that leads to death or permanent disability classified?

options.A: Mild
options.B: Expected
options.C: Tolerance
options.D: Severe

explanation: Reactions causing permanent damage, hospitalization, or death are classified as severe and require immediate reporting to keep others safe. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h6)

question: How many traditional 'rights' make up the golden rules of safe drug administration?

options.A: Ten
options.B: Seven
options.C: Three
options.D: Five

explanation: Think of the classic five: right patient, right drug, right dose, right route, and right time. Master these, and you're well on your way! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the main difference between equality and equity in healthcare?

options.A: Equity applies only to urban hospitals, while equality applies strictly to rural health posts
options.B: Equality gives everyone the same resources, while equity gives extra support to those with greater needs
options.C: Equity is decided by federal policies, while equality is managed by local community leaders
options.D: Equality focuses on curing diseases, whereas equity focuses entirely on disease prevention

explanation: Exactly! Equity recognizes that people start from different places, so we must distribute resources fairly based on actual needs to achieve true health for all. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h3)

question: In rehabilitation, what does 'empowerment' really mean for a patient?

options.A: Supporting patients and their families to make their own choices
options.B: Using expensive imported equipment for all daily exercises
options.C: Making the patient completely dependent on healthcare workers
options.D: Limiting how much a patient is involved in their care plan

explanation: Brilliant! Empowerment means walking alongside patients so they take charge of their own recovery journey instead of just waiting to be told what to do. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h2)

question: What are the two main categories of hormone disorders?

options.A: Benign or malignant
options.B: Neural or humoral
options.C: Acute or chronic
options.D: Excess or deficiency

explanation: Keep it simple: hormone problems usually happen because the body makes either too much (excess) or too little (deficiency) of a hormone. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T6#GNS211_U1_T6_h8)

question: Which hormone is famous for softening pelvic ligaments during pregnancy?

options.A: Cortisol
options.B: Relaxin
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Spot on! Relaxin lives up to its name by relaxing and loosening the ligaments to help the pelvis prepare for childbirth. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T12#GNS121_U5_T12_h2)

question: Why must anticholinergic drugs be avoided in patients with narrow-angle glaucoma?

options.A: They dilate blood vessels inside the retina
options.B: They cause permanent blindness instantly
options.C: They dissolve the cornea over time
options.D: They can dangerously increase eye pressure

explanation: Correct! Blocking acetylcholine makes the pupil widen, trapping fluid inside the eye and causing a dangerous spike in pressure. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h6)

question: Why do primary blood disorders often stress multiple organs in the body?

options.A: Because bone marrow overproduction causes physical pressure in the abdomen
options.B: Because blood circulates through every organ and delivers vital oxygen and nutrients
options.C: Because white blood cells directly attack healthy organ tissues
options.D: Because plasma proteins constantly bind to waste products

explanation: Since blood travels to every single corner of your body, any problem in the blood means every organ misses out on the oxygen and food it needs. It's a chain reaction! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T14#GNS311_U2_T14_h1)

question: Why do public health teams put exposed people in quarantine for the full incubation period?

options.A: The forced bed rest pushes the germs out of their bodies
options.B: To run expensive blood tests on everyone every single day
options.C: To watch if they fall sick before they can spread the disease
options.D: To give them routine vaccines for other sicknesses

explanation: Quarantine keeps exposed people close by until the longest expected incubation window passes, protecting others from accidental spread. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h5)

question: Which part of the brain acts as our master biological clock?

options.A: The suprachiasmatic nucleus
options.B: The pituitary gland
options.C: The cerebellum
options.D: The medulla oblongata

explanation: Think of the suprachiasmatic nucleus as your body's personal timekeeper! Located in the hypothalamus, it takes in light signals from your eyes to keep your daily body rhythms on track. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h2)

question: In which lobe of the brain is the primary somatosensory cortex located?

options.A: Occipital lobe
options.B: Parietal lobe
options.C: Frontal lobe
options.D: Temporal lobe

explanation: The primary somatosensory cortex is housed in the postcentral gyrus, which is found in the parietal lobe. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h2)

question: A doctor wants to know if a patient's low testosterone is due to a problem in the testes or the pituitary gland. Which test helps figure this out?

options.A: Serum LH and FSH hormone levels
options.B: A prostate-specific antigen blood test
options.C: A complete blood count with differential
options.D: A routine urinalysis and urine culture

explanation: Checking LH and FSH levels from the pituitary gland helps doctors see if the issue starts in the brain (pituitary) or down in the testes. Excellent clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h6)

question: Why do nurses use transmission-based precautions?

options.A: To stop the spread of specific targeted pathogens
options.B: To replace standard handwashing routines entirely
options.C: To isolate healthy staff members from routine work
options.D: To reduce hospital utility and cleaning costs

explanation: You've got this! These extra precautions are added on top of standard care whenever we are dealing with known or suspected germs that need special containment. Great job! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T10#GNS313_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why is a patient scheduled for an abdominal ultrasound usually told to fast (no food or water) for a few hours beforehand?

options.A: To keep their blood pressure steady before the scan
options.B: To cut down on tummy gas and keep the gallbladder full
options.C: To make sure they have an empty bladder for a pelvic check
options.D: To stop them from throwing up during the procedure

explanation: Food creates gas that blocks sound waves, and fasting keeps the gallbladder nice and full so it's easy to see! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h5)

question: A researcher gets a Cronbach's alpha of 0.82 for a new nursing burnout scale. What does this tell us?

options.A: The responses given by the patients are completely invalid
options.B: The questionnaire is unstable and changes too much over time
options.C: The questions on the scale measure completely different traits
options.D: The scale has strong internal consistency

explanation: Any alpha score above 0.70 is usually a green light showing your questions work well together as a team! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h4)

question: What is the very first step in the adult Chain of Survival?

options.A: Early recognition and prevention
options.B: Giving emergency medications
options.C: Advanced airway placement
options.D: Starting mouth-to-mouth rescue breathing

explanation: Spotting danger signs early helps prevent cardiac arrest before it even happens. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h1)

question: How deep should the blade go when performing a standard skin snip?

options.A: Superficially into the dermis without deep cutting
options.B: Strictly through the dead outer stratum corneum layer
options.C: Deep into the subcutaneous fat layer for fat cells
options.D: Through the entire muscle layer down to the bone

explanation: You got it! Since the little parasites hang out in the upper skin layers (dermis), we only need a very shallow snip. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h4)

question: A home health nurse notices signs of severe postpartum depression during a visit. What is the best collaborative action?

options.A: Wait until the baby is one year old before mentioning the concern.
options.B: Tell the family that mood changes always resolve completely on their own.
options.C: Refer the mother to a mental health specialist or social worker promptly.
options.D: Prescribe an antidepressant medication during the home visit.

explanation: Involving mental health professionals and social workers ensures the patient receives safe, specialized support for postpartum mood disorders. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h8)

question: Who is considered an 'informal caregiver' in elderly care?

options.A: Trainee medical students completing clinical rotations
options.B: Unpaid family members and friends who provide daily support
options.C: Hospital volunteers who visit patients on weekends
options.D: Licensed nurses who work part-time in nursing homes

explanation: Informal caregivers are usually loving relatives or friends who look after an older adult at home without getting paid. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T7#GNS321_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the main goal when a community nurse acts as an advocate for their patients?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations in local clinics
options.B: Financing private hospitals through personal funds
options.C: Enforcing strict legal penalties against sick community members
options.D: Speaking up for vulnerable groups to improve health resources

explanation: You're doing great! Being an advocate means being a voice for people who might not have the power or platform to speak up for their own health needs. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T9#GNS225_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why is sensory reception in the skin vital for overall physical safety?

options.A: It produces essential vitamins when exposed to sunlight
options.B: It warns the brain about dangerous pressure, heat, or injury
options.C: It controls how fast the outer layer of skin cells grows
options.D: It regulates the amount of water lost through the pores

explanation: Sensory receptors detect environmental hazards like extreme heat or sharp pressure so the body can react quickly. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which layer of the meninges gets its name because it looks like a spiderweb?

options.A: Periosteum
options.B: Dura mater
options.C: Arachnoid mater
options.D: Pia mater

explanation: Well done! The word 'arachnid' relates to spiders, so the web-like middle layer is named the arachnoid mater. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T8#GNS211_U3_T8_h3)

question: You want to score how well nursing students perform sterile wound dressings in simulation. Which tool fits best?

options.A: An open-ended diary for students to write about their feelings
options.B: A simple task checklist that only records yes or no without scoring
options.C: A demographic questionnaire about the students' previous degrees
options.D: An evaluation or rating checklist to score the quality of performance

explanation: A rating checklist lets you assess how *well* a skill was done, going beyond a simple yes-or-no tick. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T23#GNS224_U1_T23_h3)

question: How does yellow fever pass from one person to another?

options.A: By direct skin contact with the sweat or saliva of a carrier
options.B: By sharing eating utensils or drinking cups with an infected individual
options.C: Through the bite of an infected mosquito that previously bit a sick person
options.D: Through airborne droplets released when a patient coughs or sneezes

explanation: Spot on! Yellow fever needs a mosquito middleman—you cannot catch it just by touching or breathing near someone who is sick. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h2)

question: Why do joint contractures happen in patients with severe paralysis?

options.A: Nerves regenerate too quickly and pull the joints out of place
options.B: Joint cartilage dissolves from lack of blood circulation
options.C: Bones grow too fast because they do not bear any body weight
options.D: Muscles and tendons shorten due to a lack of movement and stretching

explanation: If a joint isn't moved through its range of motion, the soft tissues adapt by shrinking up, freezing the joint in one position. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h6)

question: Which of these is unsafe when caring for a patient with an indwelling catheter?

options.A: Keeping the drainage bag below the level of the bladder
options.B: Cleaning the perineal area and catheter tubing daily
options.C: Disconnecting the tubing frequently to let the patient walk easier
options.D: Removing the catheter as soon as it is no longer needed

explanation: Never break that closed system! Opening the tubing lets bacteria waltz right into the urinary tract. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a good strategy for helping a patient stick to a therapeutic diet long-term?

options.A: Involving family members in meal planning
options.B: Using herbs and spices to keep meals flavorful
options.C: Making gradual and sustainable food swaps
options.D: Making sudden, extreme food restrictions overnight without preparation

explanation: Going cold turkey on all your favorite foods overnight usually leads to burnout. Small, steady changes work best! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h8)

question: What is usually the very first sign that a Guinea worm is ready to come out?

options.A: A widespread rash over the entire chest and back
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin
options.C: A painful skin blister with a burning sensation
options.D: Painless swelling of the finger joints

question: Which layer of the early placental membrane eventually thins out significantly or disappears in many areas by term?

options.C: Syncytiotrophoblast
options.D: Capillary endothelium

question: Which of the following is an essential component of primary health care?

options.A: Building private pharmaceutical manufacturing plants in every town
options.B: Providing free luxury health insurance for political leaders
options.C: Performing complex open-heart surgery in rural clinics
options.D: Immunization against major infectious childhood diseases

question: Which part of a neuron usually acts like the antenna, receiving incoming signals?

options.A: Dendrites
options.B: Axon terminals
options.C: Myelin sheath
options.D: Cell body nucleus

explanation: Dendrites are the branch-like structures that reach out to catch signals from neighboring neurons and pass them toward the cell body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T6#GNS211_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why is it so helpful to check a patient's diet early on?

options.A: Predicting future genetic mutations in children
options.B: Determining the exact date of hospital discharge
options.C: Detecting nutrient deficiencies before physical signs appear
options.D: Calculating the financial cost of grocery shopping

explanation: Spotting nutrition problems early means you can jump in and help before things get worse. Excellent nursing intuition! [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h2)

question: A community health nurse is planning an outreach in a rural farming area. Which intervention targets the root cause of tapeworm spread?

options.A: Advocating for the complete ban of livestock farming in the region
options.B: Providing insect repellent sprays to prevent mosquito-borne bites
options.C: Distributing broad-spectrum antibiotics to every household in the village
options.D: Educating residents against open defecation and promoting proper meat inspection

explanation: Fantastic! Stopping open defecation and checking meat properly at abattoirs cuts the life cycle right at its source. Excellent nursing intuition! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h8)

question: A patient is recovering from a myomectomy. Which sign means you should call the doctor immediately?

options.A: Sudden severe abdominal pain and heavy vaginal bleeding
options.B: Low-grade constipation lasting twenty-four hours
options.C: A slight decrease in appetite during the first postoperative day
options.D: Mild fatigue and soreness around the surgical incision site

explanation: Sharp, severe pain and heavy bleeding after pelvic surgery are major warning signs of internal bleeding or complications that need fast medical action. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T22#GNS216_U5_T22_h7)

question: An older adult recovering from a stroke wants to dress themselves. What should you, as the home health nurse, do?

options.A: Advise the client to stay in bed until full strength returns
options.B: Provide adaptive clothing and encourage the client to dress at their own pace
options.C: Tell the family member they must dress the client every morning
options.D: Dress the client completely to save time and prevent exhaustion

explanation: Fantastic! We always want to encourage independence. Giving them the right tools and letting them take their time builds their confidence back up. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T3#GNS324_U1_T3_h2)

question: A patient with an undetectable viral load for over a year asks if they can still pass the virus sexually. What is the best response?

options.A: Transmission can only happen if they stop eating fresh fruits

options.C: Transmission is still just as likely as before starting treatment
options.D: The risk of sexual transmission is effectively zero as long as adherence is maintained

question: Which blood vessels act as control valves to regulate blood flow into local tissues?

options.A: Lymphatic ducts
options.B: Arterioles
options.C: Large arteries
options.D: Vena cavae

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take after experiencing a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Fill out an official hospital incident report form

options.C: Squeeze the wound tightly to force out as much blood as possible
options.D: Wait until the end of the shift to see if swelling develops

explanation: Immediate washing reduces the viral load introduced by the sharp object before it establishes infection. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h7)

question: What causes compartment syndrome in a patient wearing a rigid cast?

options.A: Bacterial infection develops under the padding and destroys the muscle tissue
options.B: The chemical powder used in the plaster seeps into the bloodstream and causes clotting
options.C: Swelling trapped inside a non-expanding cast puts extreme pressure on blood vessels and nerves
options.D: The patient fails to move their fingers or toes enough, causing poor circulation

explanation: Because a plaster cast can't stretch, any swelling inside builds up high pressure that squeezes the blood vessels and nerves. This is a medical emergency! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is a common reason why refugee parents might arrange an early marriage for their teenage daughter during a crisis?

options.A: They want to celebrate a lavish cultural wedding before relocating.

options.C: They receive free land ownership from the host country.

question: Why must you always wash a dirty instrument thoroughly before applying a liquid chemical disinfectant?

options.A: Physical friction is the only proven method capable of killing bacterial endospores
options.B: Organic matter like blood and mucus can block the disinfectant from reaching the microbes
options.C: Washing instruments with soap prevents the metal from rusting during the chemical soak
options.D: Cleaning chemicals neutralize the toxic residue left behind by previous sterilisation cycles

explanation: Think of dried blood or body fluids as a shield! If you don't wash them off first, the germs stay hidden and safe from your disinfectant. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why must a nurse wear PPE when performing last offices?

options.A: To protect against exposure to infectious body fluids
options.B: To comply with fire safety rules in the hospital
options.C: To prevent the family from recognizing the nurse later
options.D: To keep the nurse's uniform from getting wrinkled

explanation: Pathogens can still be present in bodily fluids after death, making standard precautions and PPE essential for staff safety. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h3)

question: What makes a piece of writing a primary literature source?

options.A: It is a textbook summary written years after the original event occurred
options.B: It is an encyclopedia entry explaining general nursing theories
options.C: It is a library catalog used to locate published journal articles
options.D: It is a first-hand account written by the researchers who conducted the study

explanation: Brilliant! Primary sources give you the raw, direct data and methods straight from the team that did the actual study. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T6#GNS217_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which factor is primarily responsible for urge faecal incontinence?

options.A: Excessive production of stomach acid
options.B: Weakened sphincters unable to hold back a strong bowel urge
options.C: Permanent blockage of the upper gastrointestinal tract
options.D: Complete absence of the large intestine

question: What is a major risk if someone takes high-dose fat-soluble vitamin supplements for months without a doctor's advice?

options.A: The excess vitamins will wash out immediately in the urine.
options.B: The kidneys will stop producing urine completely within hours.
options.C: The vitamins can accumulate in body tissues to toxic levels.
options.D: The patient will instantly develop severe iron deficiency anemia.

question: Which medication is a go-to choice for treating both bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis?

options.A: Fluconazole
options.B: Clotrimazole
options.C: Metronidazole
options.D: Acyclovir

explanation: Metronidazole is a fantastic workhorse antibiotic and anti-parasitic agent that handles both of these conditions wonderfully. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h6)

question: To diagnose Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD), how long must a patient experience excessive, hard-to-control worry?

options.A: One year
options.B: Six months
options.C: One month
options.D: Two weeks

explanation: Correct! For a GAD diagnosis, the persistent worry needs to span at least six months. Keep up the brilliant study habit! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T1#GNS324_U4_T1_h2)

question: Which sign is a classic clue that a teenager might be dealing with iron deficiency anemia?

options.A: Sudden and rapid weight gain
options.B: Hyperactive physical behavior
options.C: Yellowing of the skin and eyes
options.D: Chronic fatigue and tiredness

question: What does 'medication reconciliation' mean in home health care?

options.A: Comparing current prescribed drugs with what the patient actually takes
options.B: Disposing of all expired prescription drugs found in the bathroom
options.C: Ordering new medication supplies directly from the local pharmacy
options.D: Calculating the financial cost of monthly prescription refills

explanation: You got it! Medication reconciliation is just checking what the doctor wrote against what the patient is actually swallowing (plus any local herbs or supplements!). Keeps everyone safe. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T6#GNS324_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which adaptive tool helps a patient with shaky hands eat on their own?

options.A: A long-handled reacher
options.B: Weighted utensils
options.C: A mechanical lift
options.D: A rigid gait belt

explanation: You got it! Heavy spoons and forks help steady shaky hands so food actually makes it to the mouth. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T5#GNS123_U6_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary danger when a bleeding patient slips into hypovolemic shock?

options.B: Kidneys stop filtering waste permanently
options.C: Vital organs are starved of oxygen
options.D: Blood pressure increases too quickly

explanation: Exactly right! Losing too much blood means the heart doesn't have enough fluid to pump oxygen to major organs like the brain, heart, and kidneys. Clinical thinking looks great on you! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h3)

question: What is the most common cause of anaemia among pregnant women in Nigeria?

options.A: Rapid bone marrow aging
options.B: Not getting enough iron and folate in food
options.C: White blood cells destroying each other
options.D: Drinking too much water daily

question: What triggers the physical changes of puberty?

options.A: Hormonal surges from the endocrine system
options.B: Sudden changes in environmental temperature
options.C: Rapid expansion of skeletal muscle mass
options.D: Increased intake of dietary proteins

question: What main process causes tissue damage inside the pancreas during acute pancreatitis?

options.C: Autodigestion of the pancreas by its own early-activated enzymes
options.D: Complete lack of blood supply caused by sudden heart failure

question: A nurse notices that many mothers at a rural clinic cannot afford their babies' prescribed antibiotics. What is the best advocacy action to take?

options.A: Collaborate with social welfare services and local leaders to connect families with support programs
options.B: Pay for every patient's medications permanently out of the nurse's personal salary

options.D: Tell the mothers to stop bringing their sick children to the clinic entirely

question: Why is involving the community during the creation of IEC materials so important?

options.A: It prevents the community from ever asking questions about the disease.

question: What is your main job as a health worker when an unexpected pregnancy emergency happens in the community?

options.C: Prescribe long-term maintenance medications
options.D: Perform immediate major surgery in the village

question: Why is olfactory adaptation actually helpful for our survival?

question: What does the therapeutic use of a medication describe?

question: How do provider misconceptions about medication routes affect patient safety?

question: Which sleep stage is best known for helping the body physically recover and deeply relax its muscles?

question: What is the main job of the countercurrent multiplier in the Loop of Henle?

question: How does desmopressin help patients with mild haemophilia A or von Willebrand disease?

question: At what point must the surgical time-out be done?

question: Which type of cell division is responsible for producing sperm and egg cells?

question: Why is it important for a nurse to keep a wide stance and bend their knees when lifting or moving a patient?

question: What does 'expedited partner therapy' mean in plain nursing terms?

question: Why do doctors order genetic tests like FISH or karyotyping for blood cancers?

question: Which global agency is best known for rushing emergency food relief to disaster zones?

question: What severe reaction can happen if a hydatid cyst suddenly bursts inside the body?

question: Which of the following describes an independent double-check for high-risk medication calculations?

question: A 14-year-old pregnant patient is brought to your clinic. As her nurse, what major physical complication should you watch out for most?

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical responsibility of the nurse regarding genetic test results?

question: What is one of the most common causes of medication errors on a busy hospital ward?

question: Which type of drug reaction specifically needs the patient to have been exposed to the drug before?

options.D: Cumulative drug effect

question: If a needle absolutely must be recapped in an emergency, what is the safest way to do it?

question: What enzyme do the kidneys release when blood pressure drops too low?

question: Which genetic marker is closely linked with ankylosing spondylitis?

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand how the food supply works?

options.C: Hospitals must grow their own food to reduce patient feeding costs.

question: How has flight nursing changed from the old days to modern times?

question: What is the primary result of ignoring or banning sex education for adolescents?

question: What essential check must a nurse perform immediately after removing an IV catheter?

question: When does the postnatal period officially start?

question: A patient gets a severe wound infection three days after surgery because the instruments weren't properly sterilized. What is this called?

question: What is the main difference between a teaching method and a teaching technique in the classroom?

question: What is the medical term for the slowness of voluntary movement seen in Parkinson's patients?

options.D: Bradykinesia

question: Why do we involve family members so closely in Community-Based Rehabilitation?

options.C: Nurses prefer to avoid visiting patients at home
options.D: Community members lack basic literacy skills

explanation: Since care continues outside the hospital, family members are your greatest allies in making sure the patient keeps up with their daily exercises and routines. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h2)

question: Where are ganglia located in the human body?

options.A: Within the center of the spinal cord
options.B: Outside the central nervous system
options.C: Directly on skeletal muscle fibers
options.D: Inside the cerebral cortex only

explanation: You can picture ganglia as little relay stations located out in the peripheral nervous system, away from the brain and spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T16#GNS211_U3_T16_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of a safety box in a clinical injection setting?

options.A: To measure precise doses of liquid drugs for patients
options.B: To store brand-new, sterile syringes away from dust and moisture
options.C: To transport mixed liquid medications safely to the bedside
options.D: To safely collect used needles and syringes before disposal

explanation: Safety boxes are puncture-resistant containers built specifically to hold used sharp items and protect staff from accidental needle sticks. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h2)

question: A client in a Nigerian teaching hospital demands to see their medical case notes after a surgery. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Facilitate access to the medical records following the hospital's proper administrative process
options.B: Refuse firmly because hospital files belong exclusively to the doctors and nurses
options.C: Burn the records immediately to protect the privacy of the surgical team
options.D: Tell the client that reading medical notes is illegal for ordinary citizens

explanation: Clients have the legal right to view their own medical records through the established institutional procedures. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h3)

question: Which outcome is associated with treatment failure caused by drug resistance?

options.A: Bacterial infections disappear without any medical care
options.B: Medical costs and hospital stays decrease significantly
options.C: Infections become harder to treat with standard drugs
options.D: Patients recover much faster from common illnesses

explanation: When microbes become resistant, routine medications fail, forcing doctors to use stronger, more toxic, and costlier therapies. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h4)

question: How do daily patient payments keep the Drug Revolving Fund alive over time?

options.A: They build new residential quarters for the hospital nursing staff
options.B: They fund overseas training trips for senior medical doctors
options.C: They replace the money spent on inventory so new drugs can be bought
options.D: They pay for the electricity bills of the entire hospital complex

explanation: You got it! Patient payments replace the cash spent on the last batch of drugs, funding the very next order. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h3)

question: How should you write down a patient's story of how an injury happened in their chart?

options.A: Omitting the patient's story to save clinical documentation time
options.B: Writing down personal assumptions about the perpetrator
options.C: Using the patient's exact words in quotation marks
options.D: Summarizing the event using clinical diagnostic slang

explanation: Always use their exact words in quotes! It keeps your notes honest, clear, and legally solid. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T13#GNS312_U4_T13_h3)

question: Why are babies born to teenage mothers more likely to have a low birth weight?

options.A: Adolescent mothers usually consume excessive dietary supplements
options.B: Placental function is always enhanced in teenage pregnancies
options.C: The young mother's body is still competing for nutrients with the fetus
options.D: Fetal growth stops completely during the third trimester

explanation: Since the young mother is still growing herself, her body shares vital nutrients with the baby, often leaving both short on what they need. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T9#GNS312_U1_T9_h4)

question: What is the biggest flaw in relying too strictly on the Kubler-Ross stages?

options.A: Grief is not a rigid, universal checklist
options.B: It was proven false by lab blood tests
options.C: Patients never experience anger or depression
options.D: It only works for children with cancer

explanation: Every patient handles grief differently. Treating these stages like strict rules can make us miss the person right in front of us. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h7)

question: What is a major goal of food fortification programs in Nigeria (like adding vitamins to oil and flour)?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of hospital buildings
options.B: To replace all local staple crops with imported grains
options.C: To increase the commercial shelf life of fresh meat
options.D: To combat widespread micronutrient deficiencies

explanation: Fortifying everyday foods helps protect whole communities from missing out on key vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T005#GNS227_U4_T005_h7)

question: What is a major source of crystalline silica dust exposure for workers in many Nigerian local communities?

options.A: Operating commercial transport buses in traffic
options.B: Fishing in coastal rivers and marine lagoons
options.C: Artisanal gold mining and stone quarrying
options.D: Weaving traditional cotton fabrics by hand

explanation: Unregulated mining and quarrying activities frequently expose local Nigerian workers to high levels of dangerous silica dust. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the main health risk of breathing in silica or asbestos dust over a long time?

options.A: Progressive lung scarring and breathing damage
options.B: Severe joint pain in the fingers
options.C: Rapid hair loss and skin discoloration
options.D: Sudden hearing loss in both ears

explanation: Inhaling mineral dust causes chronic irritation and permanent scarring inside the lungs, making it much harder to breathe over time. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T5#GNS225_U7_T5_h3)

question: Why is it useful for a QA committee to compare data between day shifts and night shifts?

options.A: It ensures that doctors do not have to work during the day
options.B: It determines which shift gets paid more overtime allowances
options.C: It helps find out if fatigue or staff shortages are causing errors
options.D: It proves which nurses like working at night more

explanation: You got it! Comparing shifts helps us see if tiredness or low staffing at night affects the quality of care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h6)

question: What term describes two different observers getting similar results when watching the same event?

options.A: The Hawthorne effect
options.B: Participant bias
options.C: Inter-rater reliability
options.D: Structured validity

explanation: Well done! 'Inter-rater reliability' simply means different observers agree and are consistent in how they score what they see. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T25#GNS224_U1_T25_h5)

question: What defines gestational diabetes mellitus compared to pregestational diabetes?

options.A: It is first recognized during pregnancy
options.B: It requires permanent insulin use after delivery
options.C: It causes no risk to the developing fetus
options.D: It only occurs in women over age forty

explanation: Gestational diabetes is specifically diagnosed for the first time during the pregnant state, unlike pregestational diabetes which was present before conception. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h2)

question: What is behaviorism primarily focused on?

options.A: Observable and measurable external actions
options.B: Hidden emotional feelings and inner peace
options.C: Unconscious thoughts from childhood memories
options.D: Spiritual growth and personal reflection

explanation: Behaviorism keeps things simple: it looks only at what you can actually see and measure on the outside, rather than trying to guess inner thoughts. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h2)

question: What is the most common cause of sore and cracked nipples in a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Natural thinning of the skin during pregnancy
options.B: Drinking too little water during the day
options.C: Excessive washing of the breasts with soap
options.D: Improper latch and attachment technique

explanation: When a baby only takes the nipple instead of a large part of the areola, friction causes pain and tissue breakdown. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h6)

question: What does Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) actually measure?

options.A: The total calories burned during heavy physical exercise
options.B: The energy needed to maintain basic life functions at rest
options.C: The amount of heat produced during food digestion
options.D: The maximum oxygen consumption during endurance training

explanation: Think of BMR as your body's idle speed. It's the bare minimum energy required to keep your heart pumping, lungs breathing, and organs working while you do absolutely nothing. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T9#GNS121_U1_T9_h1)

question: An examiner is preparing to look at a patient's left eye using a direct ophthalmoscope. Which setup is correct?

options.A: Stand directly behind the patient and use both eyes at once
options.B: Rest the scope firmly against the bridge of the patient's nose
options.C: Hold the scope in the left hand and use the left eye
options.D: Hold the scope in the right hand and use the left eye

explanation: Using matching sides (left hand and left eye for the patient's left eye) allows the examiner to get close without colliding with the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is a critical safety preparation for a child dependent on a mechanical ventilator at home?

options.A: Having a backup power source and manual resuscitation bag
options.B: Relying solely on the local utility company for power alerts
options.C: Disconnecting the alarm system to maintain household quiet
options.D: Keeping the child restricted to a bed at all times

explanation: Spot on! Power cuts happen unexpectedly, so families must always have backup power and a manual bag ready for emergencies. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h5)

question: What are the three parts of the traditional epidemiological triad?

options.A: Bacteria, virus, and fungi
options.B: Patient, nurse, and doctor
options.C: Symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment
options.D: Agent, host, and environment

explanation: You will see this triad everywhere in public health! It looks at how the disease agent interacts with the vulnerable host (the person) and their surrounding environment. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T1#GNS313_U1_T1_h3)

question: Keeping a hospital patient's call bell within easy reach is an action primarily aimed at meeting which type of need?

options.A: Love and belonging
options.B: Physiological rest
options.C: Self-actualization
options.D: Safety and security

explanation: A call bell gives the patient a way to call for help, satisfying their need for physical and environmental safety. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which blood vessel brings blood directly into the glomerulus for filtering?

options.A: Peritubular capillary
options.B: Efferent arteriole
options.C: Renal vein
options.D: Afferent arteriole

explanation: Spot on! Think of the 'A' in Afferent as 'Arriving'—it brings blood into the glomerulus, while the efferent arteriole carries it away. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T6#GNS121_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is the main reason many female patients hold back from telling nurses about sexual health problems?

options.A: Feelings of embarrassment or shame
options.B: They assume doctors handle sexual topics
options.C: Insurance prevents them from talking about it
options.D: Sexual health is legally protected information

explanation: Spot on. Because of social stigma, patients often feel shy. That's why great nurses gently open the door to these topics first! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T25#GNS312_U1_T25_h5)

question: What materials are modern contraceptive diaphragms usually made of?

options.A: Silicone or latex
options.B: Rigid hard plastic
options.C: Absorbable collagen
options.D: Woven cotton mesh

explanation: Modern diaphragms use soft, flexible silicone or latex so they can comfortably bend and fit inside the vagina. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h1)

question: How does health education in the community help reduce malaria cases?

options.A: It empowers families to use preventive tools and seek early testing
options.B: It replaces the need for hospital laboratories in rural zones
options.C: It provides immediate immunity to newborns in endemic regions
options.D: It permanently eliminates mosquito breeding sites nationwide

explanation: Well done! Teaching families how to use nets properly and report fevers early stops infections before they spiral out of control. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T3#GNS214_U1_T3_h8)

question: What is the key sign that tells normal aging apart from a serious brain decline?

options.A: Preferring quiet activities over large social gatherings
options.B: Interference with daily functioning and independence
options.C: Needing reading glasses to see small text clearly
options.D: A slight increase in overall wisdom and life experience

explanation: When memory slips start getting in the way of daily living and safety, that crosses into pathological decline. Spotting this is a key nursing skill! [learn more](GNS321_U3_T3#GNS321_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why is FGM often linked to a young girl's future marriage prospects in some societies?

options.A: Uncut women are frequently labeled unmarriageable by local standards
options.B: Traditional wedding planners refuse to work with uncut families
options.C: Local marriage laws forbid ceremonies for unaltered brides
options.D: Grooms require medical certificates proving childhood surgery

explanation: Spot on! Community stigma says only cut women are worthy of marriage, pressuring families to comply. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T4#GNS312_U1_T4_h5)

question: How often should you turn an immobile, very ill patient to protect their skin?

options.A: Only when soiled
options.B: Once every shift
options.C: Every six hours
options.D: Every two hours

explanation: The golden rule of positioning! Turning patients every two hours takes the pressure off bony areas and stops bedsores before they start. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h5)

question: How does permethrin cream work against skin bugs like scabies mites and lice?

options.A: By blocking their ability to absorb oxygen through the skin
options.B: By dissolving the outer exoskeleton through extreme acidity
options.C: By stimulating the immune system to attack the eggs
options.D: By disrupting sodium channels and causing paralysis

explanation: Permethrin messes up the nerve signals in the bug's sodium channels, freezing their muscles so they become paralyzed and die. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h5)

question: Why do some disaster survivors turn to alcohol or drugs months after the event?

options.A: Because social customs require drinking alcohol during holidays
options.B: To cure physical infections caused by contaminated floodwaters
options.C: As an unhealthy attempt to self-medicate untreated emotional pain
options.D: Because emergency relief supplies always include addictive drugs

explanation: Well reasoned! When professional mental health support isn't handy, some people sadly try to use substances to numb painful memories and calm their anxiety. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h6)

question: What is the best way to determine a patient's prior knowledge about a new medication?

options.A: Asking open-ended questions
options.B: Ordering a blood electrolyte panel
options.C: Reading their bank statements
options.D: Checking their vital signs

explanation: Open-ended questions invite patients to share what they understand in their own words without feeling tested. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h3)

question: During a routine screening test where the cervix is inspected visually using acetic acid (VIA), what is acetic acid actually made of?

options.C: Betadine solution
options.D: Hydrogen peroxide

question: What is a major economic reason why impoverished households practice child marriage?

options.A: Complying with mandatory government taxation policies for unmarried girls

options.C: Funding the higher education of male siblings in the family
options.D: Reducing household financial burdens through bride price or fewer dependents

explanation: Extreme poverty pushes some families to marry off young daughters to ease household expenses and sometimes gain financial help through bride wealth. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h2)

question: Why are weight-bearing joints like the knees and hips so prone to physical stress?

options.A: They rely only on skin and fat for stability
options.B: They lack any form of cartilage protection
options.C: They must support body weight while managing movement forces
options.D: They are completely fused and cannot absorb shock

explanation: Exactly! Our knees and hips carry gravity's load all day while taking the pounding of walking and running, leading to natural wear over time. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h4)

question: A patient presents with extreme fatigue, pale skin, and spoon-shaped fingernails. Which deficiency is most likely present?

options.B: Calcium
options.C: Thiamine
options.D: Iron

question: Which chemical messenger in the brain ramps up electrical activity during a seizure?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Serotonin
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Glutamate

explanation: Spot on! Glutamate is the main 'gas pedal' neurotransmitter that drives excessive brain cell firing during a seizure. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T10#GNS222_U4_T10_h2)

question: A patient arrives at the emergency ward with a high fever, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, and tummy pain after a clandestine abortion. What is your top nursing priority?

options.A: Immediate scheduling for cosmetic scar revision
options.B: Documenting the identity of the illegal practitioner
options.C: Counseling on future contraceptive methods
options.D: Systemic sepsis and infection management

question: How do intravenous (IV) fluids like normal saline help a patient with severe fluid loss?

options.A: They dissolve blockages in the coronary arteries

options.C: They restore circulating blood volume inside the vessels
options.D: They replace lost vitamins in the muscle tissue

question: Which of the following is a common misconception about modern contraceptives?

options.C: They always cure infectious diseases instantly
options.D: They make hair grow faster all over the body

question: What is a normal, expected sensation for a patient receiving intravenous contrast dye during a CT scan?

options.C: Extreme drowsiness and deep sleep
options.D: A warm flushing feeling over the body

question: What actually happens during an intrauterine insemination (IUI) procedure?

question: Why is it so helpful for a nurse to explain health concepts in local languages?

options.C: It speeds up the process of writing patient case notes
options.D: It helps patients understand and apply health practices

explanation: When you speak in familiar terms, patients truly grasp the message and can easily act on it. Communication is key to great nursing! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of rectovaginal fistula?

options.C: Inflammatory bowel diseases like Crohn's
options.D: Surgical complications from perineal repair

question: What is the main difference between a PET scan and a standard CT or MRI scan?

options.A: A PET scan takes only a few seconds while CT and MRI take hours.

options.C: A PET scan shows cellular function while CT and MRI mainly show body structures.
options.D: A PET scan is completely painless while CT and MRI cause physical discomfort.

explanation: You got it! PET scans look at how cells are working and using energy (metabolism), while regular scans like CT and MRI are more like cameras taking sharp pictures of your body's anatomy and physical structures. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h1)

question: Why do mothers who have given birth before (multiparous women) often feel stronger afterpains than first-time mothers?

options.A: Their perineal wounds are always surgically larger
options.B: They are more sensitive to standard doses of analgesics
options.C: They produce significantly less lochia than primiparous mothers
options.D: Their uterine muscles lose tone and contract intermittently with greater force

question: Why is multi-sectoral collaboration necessary for executing a national population policy?

options.A: Local governments have no role in community development.
options.B: Only one government ministry is allowed to handle population matters.
options.C: NGOs and traditional rulers are legally banned from healthcare.
options.D: Population issues impact health, education, and economic sectors simultaneously.

explanation: Population touches everything—health, schools, jobs, and social welfare. Because of this, different sectors and leaders must team up to make real progress. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T007#GNS226_U6_T007_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of a geriatric home?

options.A: Providing daycare services exclusively for working parents
options.B: Offering temporary quarantine for infectious diseases
options.C: Serving as a permanent substitute for acute surgical hospitals
options.D: Providing specialized residential care for older adults

explanation: Geriatric homes are set up to look after older adults who need a bit of help with their daily activities. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T13#GNS324_U5_T13_h1)

question: In family planning clinics, how do we define a 'new acceptor'?

options.A: A nurse newly transferred to manage the reproductive health unit

options.C: A client adopting a modern contraceptive method for the first time

question: What is the medical term for those sudden waves of intense body heat and flushing?

options.B: Peripheral neuropathy
options.C: Vasomotor symptoms
options.D: Genitourinary syndrome

question: What is the single best way to stop germs from spreading when handling specimens?

options.A: Changing the patient room air filters daily
options.B: Wearing two pairs of sterile gloves at all times
options.C: Spraying the examination table with bleach
options.D: Proper hand hygiene before and after the procedure

explanation: Simple handwashing remains your greatest superpower in infection control. Wash your hands religiously! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T4#GNS112_U6_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the standard core rights of medication administration?

question: Why is palliative care introduced early for patients with inherited degenerative conditions?

options.A: To shorten the overall duration of the chronic disease process

options.C: To immediately stop all medical therapies and disease-specific medications
options.D: To focus on symptom relief and quality of life alongside active treatment

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for the very end; it's all about keeping the patient comfortable, happy, and pain-free right from diagnosis. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h7)

question: What key lifestyle advice should a nurse include when educating a patient with prediabetes?

options.B: Sleep for at least fourteen hours every single night
options.C: Incorporate a balanced diet and regular physical activity
options.D: Eliminate all forms of water from the daily diet

question: What is the main way injectable contraceptives prevent pregnancy in the body?

options.C: Lowering total estrogen production in the adrenal glands
options.D: Stopping the release of an egg from the ovary

question: What does drug tolerance mean?

options.A: Having an allergic skin rash develop after starting a new prescription
options.B: The body clearing the medication from the kidneys within minutes
options.C: Experiencing severe tremors immediately after taking a single pill
options.D: Needing larger doses of a drug over time to get the same physical effect

question: What is your very first nursing action if a patient gets a chemical splash in their eye?

options.C: Cover the eye with a dry cotton pad and wait

question: While looking at an ovary slide under a microscope, you spot a large fluid-filled space called an antrum. What kind of follicle is this?

question: Which drug is a main part of the preferred first-line HIV treatment guidelines in Nigeria?

options.C: Zidovudine
options.D: Nevirapine

question: Why are anticholinergic drugs sometimes given to patients right before surgery?

options.B: To lower the patient's blood pressure
options.C: To completely paralyze skeletal muscles
options.D: To induce deep general anesthesia
