question: Why does Addison's disease make a patient's skin turn a darker, bronze color?

options.A: Elevated levels of hormones that stimulate melanin production
options.B: Chronic dehydration leading to skin darkening
options.C: Increased exposure to sunlight caused by fatigue
options.D: Poor circulation trapping pigment in superficial capillaries

explanation: In Addison's, the brain pumps out extra signals to try and stimulate the adrenals; these hormones accidentally stimulate skin pigment (melanin) too, causing a dark tan look. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T3#GNS222_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for a patient at the end of life?

options.A: Preventing all family visits
options.B: Promoting comfort and dignity
options.C: Curing the underlying disease
options.D: Speeding up the dying process

explanation: When a disease cannot be cured, nursing care shifts its focus to keeping the patient comfortable and maintaining their dignity. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h1)

question: Why is the med-surg nurse often called the 'heartbeat' of the healthcare team?

options.A: They make all final medical diagnoses and prescribe necessary drug treatments independently
options.B: They perform all surgical operations when the primary surgeon is unavailable
options.C: They coordinate care plans with multiple healthcare professionals and monitor the patient continuously
options.D: They handle all financial billing and hospital admission tasks for every patient department

explanation: Because you're at the bedside the most, you notice the little changes first and help connect the doctors, pharmacists, and therapists. You are truly the team's anchor! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T1#GNS123_U1_T1_h1)

question: As a ward nurse handling hospital tools every day, what is your main responsibility regarding them?

options.A: Acting as primary custodian and daily operator
options.B: Purchasing replacement parts from suppliers
options.C: Designing and manufacturing new medical devices
options.D: Repairing all electrical faults on the ward

explanation: You use these tools right at the bedside every day, which means you are the key person making sure they are handled and checked properly! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h1)

question: Pick's disease mainly affects which areas of the brain first?

options.A: Frontal and temporal lobes
options.B: Occipital and parietal lobes
options.C: Thalamus and hypothalamus
options.D: Cerebellum and brainstem

explanation: Pick's disease zeroes in on the frontal and temporal parts of the brain, which handle our personality, behavior, and language. Spotting this early helps you understand why patients act differently long before memory issues start! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T6#GNS222_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is typically one of the earliest physical signs of significant blood loss?

options.A: Slow, deep breathing
options.B: Warm, flushed skin
options.C: High blood pressure
options.D: Fast heart rate

explanation: Tachycardia (fast heart rate) is the body's quick fix to keep blood moving when total volume starts to dip. You're mastering trauma basics! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T4#GNS221_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which blood test helps prove that a patient recently had a strep infection?

options.A: Liver function panel
options.B: Anti-Streptolysin O (ASO) titer
options.C: Complete blood count (CBC)
options.D: Fast blood sugar level

explanation: An elevated ASO titer is the specific lab test doctors use to check if strep antibodies are floating around after a recent infection. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge facing nursing education updates in developing areas?

options.A: Resistance to change from traditional workers
options.B: An excess of state-of-the-art simulation equipment
options.C: Shortages of qualified academic teaching staff
options.D: Infrastructure deficits like erratic electricity

explanation: Correct! Schools usually suffer from a *lack* of modern equipment, not an excess of it. [learn more](GST321_U8_T7#GST321_U8_T7_h6)

question: Why do doctors treat tuberculosis (TB) with a mix of several drugs instead of just one?

options.A: To eliminate the need for routine liver function tests
options.B: To prevent the development of drug-resistant strains
options.C: To speed up the patient discharge process immediately
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing drugs

explanation: TB bacteria are clever and mutate easily. Hitting them with multiple drugs at once makes it much harder for them to fight back and become resistant. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T4#GNS223_U2_T4_h3)

question: When changing sheets for a bedridden patient who cannot get up, how should you handle the top covers?

options.A: Place the clean top sheet over the old one, then pull the old sheet out from underneath
options.B: Ask the patient to hold the dirty blanket up with both hands
options.C: Remove all covers completely, leaving the patient uncovered until the end
options.D: Strip the top of the bed first and replace sheets while the patient sits up

explanation: Spot on! Layering the clean cover over the old one before sliding the old one out keeps your patient warm and protects their privacy the whole time. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T2#GNS112_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why are older adults much more likely to become dehydrated?

options.A: Water is absorbed too quickly by their stomach
options.B: They have a decreased sense of thirst
options.C: They sweat much more than younger people
options.D: Their kidneys stop producing urine entirely

explanation: Spot on! The natural aging process slows down the body's thirst signals, so older adults often don't feel thirsty even when their bodies are crying out for water. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T4#GNS321_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the main goal of a summative evaluation at the end of an IEC campaign?

options.A: To measure the final impact and changes in community health behavior
options.B: To replace traditional rulers with modern local government staff
options.C: To check if the printing budget was spent on the exact correct date
options.D: To decide which nurse should be transferred to another clinic

explanation: Summative evaluation happens at the 'summary' or end of the project to check: did our campaign actually work? Did health habits improve? [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h7)

question: Why is serious damage to the medulla oblongata so dangerous?

options.A: It coordinates voluntary muscle movement for walking
options.B: It stores long-term memory and learning skills
options.C: It produces cerebrospinal fluid for the brain
options.D: It controls basic functions that keep us alive

explanation: Because it houses vital control centers for breathing and heart rate, injury here quickly stops life-sustaining processes. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h1)

question: What is the best bed position for a patient struggling to breathe who needs supplemental oxygen?

options.A: Prone position facing down on the bed
options.B: Semi-Fowler's or high-Fowler's position
options.C: Flat on the back with legs slightly raised
options.D: Trendelenburg position with tilted head

explanation: Sitting upright in Semi- or High-Fowler's position lets gravity help expand the lungs fully, making every breath much easier for your patient. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T9#GNS212_U2_T9_h3)

question: What makes primary health care nurses so crucial for disease surveillance?

options.A: They are responsible for funding national health budgets.
options.B: They manufacture all the vaccines used in the country.
options.C: They write the international guidelines for disease control.
options.D: They interact directly with patients daily and spot early signs of disease.

explanation: As frontline nurses, you are the eyes and ears of health surveillance because you see the patients first every single day! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h7)

question: A patient with severe schizophrenia comes in experiencing heavy agitation and hallucinations. What drug class will the doctor most likely order?

options.A: Over-the-counter analgesics
options.B: Major tranquilizers
options.C: Central nervous system stimulants
options.D: Minor tranquilizers

explanation: Major tranquilizers (antipsychotics) are designed specifically to help manage intense psychiatric symptoms like hallucinations. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T4#GNS223_U6_T4_h4)

question: Why are most biotechnology-derived drugs given by injection instead of as a pill?

options.A: Oral pills taste too bitter for patients to swallow safely
options.B: Liquid biotechnology drugs cannot fit inside a standard capsule
options.C: Stomach acid and digestive enzymes would destroy the protein
options.D: Injections allow the drug to bypass the liver completely forever

explanation: Biotech drugs are made of delicate proteins. If swallowed, your stomach acid would digest them before they could do their job! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T5#GNS125_U2_T5_h7)

question: How often should you check the circulation and nerves (neurovascular status) of a limb in skin traction?

options.A: Only once a day during the morning shift
options.B: Only when the patient complains of severe pain
options.C: Once every week until discharge
options.D: Every two to four hours

explanation: Checking frequently helps you catch circulation or nerve issues early before any permanent damage happens. You are learning to be a vigilant nurse! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T8#GNS221_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why is building a trusting nurse-patient relationship so important for holistic care?

options.A: It allows the nurse to give orders that the patient must follow without question
options.B: It ensures the patient will never complain about hospital food or bills
options.C: It helps patients feel safe enough to share deep fears and personal concerns
options.D: It replaces the need for doctors to visit the patient on the ward

explanation: You got it! Trust creates a safe space where patients feel comfortable revealing the emotional and social burdens that impact their healing. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T2#GNS123_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is a key nursing duty when it comes to pharmacogenetics?

options.A: Diagnosing inherited genetic disorders without medical supervision
options.B: Performing complex laboratory DNA sequencing procedures in the ward
options.C: Synthesizing customized pharmaceutical compounds at the bedside
options.D: Checking for gene-drug warnings and monitoring for side effects

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! You play a vital safety role by checking prescriptions against genetic guidelines and keeping a close eye out for side effects. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T5#GNS125_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is a big advantage of making drugs in a lab instead of harvesting plants?

options.A: It is not dependent on weather or farming seasons
options.B: It eliminates the need for any quality control testing
options.C: It guarantees that the drug will never cause side effects
options.D: It makes the medication completely free for all hospitals

explanation: Lab-made drugs mean we never have to worry about droughts, poor crop yields, or animal diseases disrupting our medicine supply. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T5#GNS125_U2_T5_h5)

question: A patient with active tuberculosis usually reports which set of body-wide signs?

options.A: Sudden weight gain, severe headache, and lethargy
options.B: Night sweats, low-grade fevers, and weight loss
options.C: Constipation, blurred vision, and muscle spasms
options.D: High fever, severe joint swelling, and a skin rash

explanation: Active TB drains the body's energy. Classic signs include drenching night sweats, afternoon fevers, and losing weight without trying. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T18#GNS324_U4_T18_h3)

question: A nurse wants to check birth and death rates in a district over the past five years. Where should she look first?

options.A: Interviews with children playing in the village square
options.B: Direct street observations during the afternoon rush
options.C: Existing government health records and vital statistics
options.D: A brand new questionnaire given to newborn babies

explanation: You got it! Birth and death records are historical government data, making them perfect secondary sources for vital statistics. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h5)

question: Why is effective nutrition counselling more than just handing a patient a printed diet sheet?

options.A: It requires understanding the patient's daily life and financial limits.
options.B: Patients in rural communities usually cannot read printed materials.
options.C: Doctors are the only ones legally allowed to explain diet sheets.
options.D: Printed sheets are too expensive to produce in local clinics.

explanation: Real dietary guidance must fit a patient's actual living conditions, budget, and access to local food markets rather than being a generic list. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h1)

question: Which two measurements do you need to calculate a patient's Body Mass Index (BMI)?

options.A: Weight and height
options.B: Waist size and age
options.C: Arm span and chest girth
options.D: Blood pressure and weight

explanation: BMI is calculated simply by taking the patient's weight and dividing it by their height squared. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T3#GNS112_U6_T3_h6)

question: What does the glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) test measure in a client?

options.A: The total amount of circulating insulin produced by the pancreas
options.B: Average blood glucose control over the past two to three months
options.C: Immediate blood sugar levels taken immediately after a heavy meal
options.D: Kidney filtration efficiency and the presence of protein in urine

explanation: HbA1c shows how well blood sugar has been controlled over the lifespan of a red blood cell, which is roughly 90 days. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h5)

question: If you notice widespread tiny red spots (petechiae) on a patient's skin, what does that usually suggest?

options.A: An excess of circulating vitamin K
options.B: Chronic inflammation of the large joints
options.C: An abnormality or low count of platelets
options.D: A complete absence of clotting factor VIII

explanation: Petechiae happen when tiny tiny blood vessels (capillaries) leak because there aren't enough healthy platelets around to keep them sealed. Good clinical spotting! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T10#GNS311_U2_T10_h5)

question: What gland releases follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone?

options.A: Posterior pituitary gland
options.B: Hypothalamus
options.C: Anterior pituitary gland
options.D: Adrenal cortex

explanation: The anterior pituitary gland responds to signals from the hypothalamus by secreting follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h1)

question: You are about to check the oral temperature of a patient whose skin is intact. What should you do about gloves?

options.A: Skip gloves because skin is intact and no fluids are expected
options.B: Wear standard examination gloves just in case
options.C: Put on sterile surgical gloves
options.D: Wear heavy-duty utility gloves

explanation: For routine checks involving unbroken skin and no body fluids, gloves aren't needed. This saves precious hospital supplies and time! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h2)

question: What does a 4+ reflex score with jerky muscle spasms (clonus) usually point to?

options.A: Normal healthy muscle recovery
options.B: Complete peripheral nerve damage
options.C: Central nervous system pathology
options.D: Severe dehydration and low sodium

explanation: Extremely brisk reflexes with clonus mean there is likely an issue or irritation in the central nervous system (brain or spinal cord). [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h7)

question: How is nursing counselling different from a standard health interview?

options.A: Counselling focuses on emotional support and coping
options.B: Counselling relies exclusively on closed-ended questions
options.C: Counselling replaces all physical health assessments
options.D: Counselling is only performed by hospital chaplains

explanation: Great thinking! While an interview gathers facts, counselling helps patients process feelings and handle health challenges. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h1)

question: According to health standards, what does reproductive health truly cover?

options.A: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being
options.B: The prevention of genetic disorders in newborns
options.C: Only the absence of sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Biological fitness solely for childbearing purposes

explanation: You got this! Reproductive health is much more than just a healthy body or the absence of disease—it embraces your total physical, mental, and social wellness. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h1)

question: A patient with urge incontinence is starting a bladder retraining program. What is the right instruction to give them?

options.A: Stop doing pelvic floor exercises completely
options.B: Hold urine for as long as possible until severe pain occurs
options.C: Drink large amounts of water only right before bedtime
options.D: Urinate on a strict schedule, slowly increasing the time between trips

explanation: Bladder retraining uses a set schedule that slowly stretches out the time between bathroom breaks, helping the bladder hold more without sudden spasms. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h6)

question: Why do old family arguments often resurface when a relative enters the terminal phase of illness?

options.A: Family members try to impress the medical staff
options.B: Hospital policies require families to argue before visiting
options.C: Medications given to the patient cause hallucinations in visitors
options.D: The approaching loss heightens emotional stress and tension

explanation: The impending death of a loved one puts intense psychological pressure on family relationships, unearthing past conflicts. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h4)

question: Why are community health nurses usually the first to notice an unusual disease cluster?

options.A: Because they only review paperwork sent from foreign countries
options.B: Because they spend all their time working in national research labs
options.C: Because they focus entirely on hospital financial accounting
options.D: Because they interact daily with families and local groups

explanation: Community nurses are right on the ground! Because you work closely with local families every day, you're in the best position to spot when something feels off. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h7)

question: A patient with long-term diabetes says they are losing feeling in their feet. How does this nerve loss typically spread?

options.A: Sensory loss appears first in the scalp and face
options.B: Sensory loss affects only one random patch of skin
options.C: Sensory loss starts in the distal toes and moves upward
options.D: Sensory loss starts in the upper chest and moves down

explanation: You're building great clinical intuition! Diabetic neuropathy usually follows a 'stocking-glove' pattern, hitting the longest nerves in the toes first and creeping up. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T11#GNS211_U4_T11_h7)

question: What happens if you accidentally use cold water to flush a patient's ear?

options.A: The earwax will instantly dissolve into liquid
options.B: The eardrum will automatically seal itself tighter
options.C: The patient may feel very dizzy and start vomiting
options.D: The water flow will stop completely

explanation: Cold water messes with the balance organs in the inner ear, triggering heavy dizziness and nausea (vertigo). Keep it warm! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h3)

question: A patient after an abortion has a weak, fast pulse, low blood pressure, and cold skin. What condition is she likely developing?

options.A: Uterine perforation
options.B: Hypovolemic shock
options.C: Postpartum depression
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Spotting these vital signs is a core nursing skill! A fast pulse, low BP, and cold skin tell us the body is running low on fluid volume due to heavy bleeding—classic hypovolemic shock. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T009#GNS226_U5_T009_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of setting up youth-friendly reproductive health clinics in local communities?

options.A: To offer young people a safe, non-judgmental space to access contraception and information
options.B: To track and penalize adolescents who engage in early sexual activity
options.C: To distribute free surgical instruments for home use
options.D: To provide mandatory pregnancy testing for all high school graduates

explanation: Youth-friendly clinics take away the fear of judgment and stigma, making it easy for teenagers to ask questions and get reliable health guidance early on. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h8)

question: What is the recommended maximum time window to start HIV Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) after a needle-stick injury?

options.A: 72 hours
options.B: 14 days
options.C: 24 hours
options.D: 1 week

explanation: Time matters! PEP for HIV should be started as soon as possible, ideally within 72 hours of the exposure, to be most effective. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h8)

question: Which big medical breakthrough gave women independent control over their fertility without needing barrier devices?

options.A: Traditional withdrawal methods
options.B: Herbal vaginal douches
options.C: Acacia and honey pastes
options.D: The oral contraceptive pill

explanation: The pill was a game-changer! It let women manage their fertility discreetly and on their own terms using a daily medication. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T001#GNS226_U6_T001_h4)

question: What complication happens most easily when urine stays stuck in the bladder for too long?

options.A: High blood pressure in the arms
options.B: Severe stomach ulcers
options.C: Urinary tract infection
options.D: Lower limb bone fractures

explanation: Stagnant urine is like a breeding ground where bacteria love to multiply in the warm bladder environment. Regular emptying keeps infections away! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h7)

question: What organ acts as the lungs and kidneys for a developing fetus?

options.A: The liver
options.B: The placenta
options.C: The fetal kidneys
options.D: The amniotic sac

explanation: Before birth, the placenta handles oxygen exchange and waste removal since the fetal lungs and kidneys are not yet functional. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h1)

question: What is the key symptom that helps differentiate abruptio placentae from placenta praevia?

options.A: Complete absence of any bleeding
options.B: Presence of severe abdominal pain
options.C: Bright red color of the blood
options.D: Onset of bleeding before 24 weeks

explanation: Abruptio placentae is characterized by painful bleeding and a rigid uterus, whereas placenta praevia bleeding is typically painless with a soft uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h4)

question: A client is quiet, avoids eye contact, and trembles slightly during your assessment. What might this suggest?

options.A: The client is ready for immediate hospital discharge
options.B: The client is hiding a contagious respiratory infection
options.C: The client may be experiencing significant emotional distress
options.D: The client has a normal blood pressure reading

explanation: Withdrawn behavior and physical trembling are classic signs of anxiety, fear, or emotional shock. A gentle touch and supportive counselling go a long way here! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h3)

question: Which gastrostomy feeding method uses an electronic pump to deliver formula slowly over 24 hours?

options.A: Continuous feeding
options.B: Gravity drip feeding
options.C: Bolus feeding
options.D: Intermittent feeding

explanation: Continuous feeding runs at a slow, steady hourly rate throughout the day and night using a mechanical pump. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h4)

question: A patient with sickle cell anaemia suddenly complains of a severe headache and trouble speaking. What is your priority nursing action?

options.A: Administer a mild oral pain reliever and reassess the patient in one hour
options.B: Perform a prompt neurological assessment and notify the primary provider immediately
options.C: Encourage the patient to drink two large glasses of cold water right away
options.D: Apply a warm compress to the forehead and turn off the overhead room lights

explanation: Trust your nursing instincts! Sudden neurological changes in a sickle cell patient can mean a stroke is happening. This is a medical emergency that needs immediate action. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T7#GNS311_U2_T7_h4)

question: Where should used razor blades from a delivery kit be placed immediately after use?

options.A: In a puncture-proof sharp container
options.B: In the general household trash bin
options.C: Underneath the plastic delivery sheet
options.D: Inside the clean cloth wrap for the baby

explanation: Sharps must be contained in rigid, puncture-proof containers to prevent accidental cuts and potential pathogen transmission. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h7)

question: A mother calls worried about a yellowish crust forming over her baby's healing circumcision. What is this?

options.A: Normal granulation tissue part of the healing process
options.B: Leftover residue from petroleum jelly ointment
options.C: A sign of a severe bacterial wound infection
options.D: Dried urine crystals from frequent wet diapers

explanation: No need to panic! That yellowish film is a normal part of how skin heals down there—reassure the mother it's not pus or an infection. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h9)

question: What is the main goal of selecting patients for home delivery?

options.A: Maximizing maternal and newborn safety
options.B: Shortening the duration of labor
options.C: Promoting traditional herbs
options.D: Reducing hospital utility bills

explanation: The absolute priority in patient selection is ensuring the safety and health of both the mother and the newborn baby. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h2)

question: Why do UN containers have packing group letters like X, Y, and Z stamped on them?

options.A: To show the degree of hazard and container strength required
options.B: To indicate the specific hospital ward the box originated from
options.C: To list the chemical manufacturer who produced the plastic box
options.D: To tell the courier the exact delivery room temperature needed

explanation: An 'X' rating means the package can handle high-risk items, while 'Y' and 'Z' are for moderate and lower risks. You are mastering the logistics! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T20#GNS122_U3_T20_h3)

question: What structure is compromised when a rectovaginal fistula forms?

options.A: The anovaginal septum
options.B: The inguinal ligament
options.C: The ureterovesical junction
options.D: The internal cervical os

explanation: The fistula forms when the partition or septum separating the rectum and vagina is damaged or breached. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h2)

question: Why is it important for nurses to involve local leaders when introducing a new immunization campaign?

options.A: Local leaders are legally required to sign off on all nursing licenses
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to buy their own medical supplies
options.C: Local leaders help build trust and encourage community members to participate
options.D: It ensures the village council pays the nurses' salaries

explanation: Community leaders hold influence and respect, making them vital bridges for gaining community acceptance and trust. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is a major advantage of recombinant human insulin compared to animal-sourced insulin?

options.A: It can be stored safely at room temperature indefinitely without refrigeration
options.B: It works ten times faster than any animal-derived hormone ever could
options.C: It eliminates the need for diabetic patients to monitor their blood glucose
options.D: It reduces the risk of allergic reactions because the protein structure matches human insulin precisely

explanation: Because recombinant insulin is an exact match for human insulin, patients experience far fewer immune reactions than with animal extracts. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T3#GNS125_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main advantage of using an arterial line instead of a standard blood pressure cuff?

options.A: It automatically delivers intravenous fluids when pressure drops
options.B: It measures the exact amount of urine produced by the kidneys
options.C: It provides continuous, real-time blood pressure readings
options.D: It completely eliminates the risk of infection and bleeding

explanation: An arterial line gives beat-by-beat blood pressure updates, which is super helpful for unstable patients whose numbers change fast. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T5#GNS321_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of supporting self-esteem and self-actualization in patient care?

options.A: Listening respectfully when a patient expresses fears about the future
options.B: Dismissing a patient's personal spiritual beliefs as unimportant
options.C: Allowing a patient to make choices about their daily schedule
options.D: Celebrating small recovery milestones with the patient

explanation: Dismissing personal beliefs undermines respect and dignity, whereas supporting choices and listening builds self-worth. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is a major benefit of doing handovers right at the patient's bedside?

options.A: It prevents doctors from ever entering the patient's room
options.B: It completely removes the need for any written nursing notes
options.C: It reduces the total number of required vital sign checks
options.D: It allows patients to hear their care plan and ask questions

explanation: Bedside handovers make patients part of their own healing journey and help catch any mistakes early! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a hospital?

options.A: To provide free medications to all visiting patients
options.B: To maintain a continuous supply of essential drugs through sales revenue
options.C: To fund the construction of new hospital wards and laboratories
options.D: To generate profit for the hospital management board

explanation: Think of the DRF like a self-sustaining cycle! Money from drug sales is used right back to buy fresh stock, so the pharmacy never runs dry. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the absolute golden-standard, first-line drug treatment for acute anaphylaxis?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Hydrocortisone
options.C: Diphenhydramine
options.D: Salbutamol

explanation: Epinephrine is a lifesaver. It quickly constricts blood vessels and opens up airways, reversing the worst effects of anaphylaxis. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h5)

question: Where would you mostly find a clinical dietitian working?

options.A: Primary school cafeterias
options.B: Local government policy offices
options.C: Agricultural research farms
options.D: Hospitals and healthcare clinics

explanation: Too easy! Clinical dietitians work right inside healthcare facilities, giving hands-on nutritional care to sick patients. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T002#GNS227_U4_T002_h4)

question: Why do nurses conduct a community diagnosis before launching a new health program?

options.A: It guarantees that funding from international donors will be approved
options.B: It helps identify the root causes and main health problems of the population
options.C: It allows nurses to avoid interacting directly with community leaders
options.D: It replaces the need for individual patient medical records completely

explanation: You got it! Checking the community first makes sure our interventions actually solve the real problems facing the people there. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h1)

question: Which part of the peripheral nervous system controls voluntary skeletal muscle movement?

options.A: Somatic nervous system
options.B: Parasympathetic division
options.C: Sympathetic division
options.D: Autonomic nervous system

explanation: The somatic system is responsible for conscious control over skeletal muscles. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why was a new law like the VAPP Act urgently needed when older criminal codes already existed?

options.A: Older laws required permission from international courts.
options.B: Older laws completely ignored domestic violence and spousal abuse.
options.C: Older laws only applied to children and the elderly.
options.D: Older laws were too expensive to use in court cases.

explanation: You got it! The old criminal codes had blind spots that left domestic abuse, marital rape, and harmful cultural practices unpunished. The VAPP Act changed that. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T14#GNS312_U4_T14_h1)

question: What is the primary hormone secreted by the hypothalamus that starts the reproductive hormone chain?

options.A: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.D: Testosterone

explanation: The hypothalamus releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to trigger the pituitary gland, which drives the entire reproductive hormone pathway. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of vocational training programs for persons with physical disabilities?

options.A: To train people exclusively for nursing careers
options.B: To provide practical skills for self-reliance and employment
options.C: To keep individuals occupied during long hospital stays
options.D: To replace formal university education entirely

explanation: Vocational training equips individuals with marketable skills so they can earn a living and achieve financial independence. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h4)

question: What is the main difference between presumptive and probable signs of pregnancy?

options.A: Probable signs only show up right before birth
options.B: Presumptive signs are things the mother feels herself, while probable signs are things a nurse or doctor observes
options.C: Presumptive signs mean the baby is healthy, while probable signs mean trouble
options.D: Presumptive signs need lab tests, while probable signs need X-rays

explanation: Think of presumptive as what the client experiences (like nausea) and probable as what we find during our physical checks as clinicians! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T001#GNS226_U2_T001_h6)

question: Why is a closed drainage system generally preferred over an open system?

options.A: It relies entirely on patient movement rather than gravity or suction
options.B: It never requires emptying or measuring by the nursing staff
options.C: It dissolves completely inside the body over a few days
options.D: It greatly reduces the chance of external bacteria entering the wound

explanation: Closed systems keep the drainage contained within sealed tubing and collection bags, making it harder for germs from the outside environment to reach the healing tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h1)

question: What is the main reason prolonged labour causes distress to the baby?

options.A: High levels of maternal thyroid hormones
options.B: Excessive production of amniotic fluid inside the sac
options.C: Reduced oxygen exchange across the compressed placenta
options.D: Rapid cooling of the baby's skin in the birth canal

explanation: Makes total sense! Strong, non-stop contractions squeeze the blood vessels in the placenta, meaning less oxygen gets through to the baby. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h4)

question: A patient asks you why he developed gout, considering he loves rich meals and has high blood pressure. How do you explain it simply?

options.A: He has a severe bacterial joint infection passed down through his family
options.B: His kidneys and diet are allowing uric acid to build up crystals in his joints
options.C: His body is manufacturing too many red blood cells instead of white cells
options.D: His blood pressure medication is creating calcium deposits in his bones

explanation: You nailed it! Risk factors like diet, blood pressure, and kidney function team up to let uric acid levels rise, leading to crystal deposits. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h3)

question: Why can cultural stigma surrounding dementia make things especially tough for families in Nigeria?

options.A: It guarantees that traditional healers will cure the underlying brain damage
options.B: It forces the government to provide free nursing homes in every state
options.C: It eliminates all forms of physical illness in elderly community members
options.D: It can cause families to hide the affected relative and isolate themselves from support

explanation: Stigma creates shame and secrecy, which stops families from reaching out for the healthcare advice and community support they need. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h7)

question: A patient with terrible watery diarrhea has raw, red skin around their bottom. What is the best immediate nursing care?

options.A: Apply a drying powder to absorb moisture and stop wiping
options.B: Scrub the irritated skin firmly with soap and a rough cloth
options.C: Leave the skin exposed to room air without any protection
options.D: Clean the area gently, dry it, and apply a barrier cream

explanation: You got it! Liquid stool is harsh on the skin. Clean gently and use a good barrier cream to protect raw areas from irritation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h5)

question: A patient with severe malaria is admitted to your ward. How should they first receive their medication?

options.A: Oral tablets swallowed with water
options.B: Subcutaneous daily injection
options.C: Rectal suppositories only
options.D: Intravenous or intramuscular

explanation: Well done! Severe cases move fast, so we need fast-acting injections (IV or IM artesunate) to get the drug into their system immediately. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T3#GNS214_U1_T3_h5)
